gate.note: v1.2 (10/12/2026): the model now fits one detection efficiency per observing program (NASA, MIDAS, UEC, NELIOTA, TILT, LUMIO) and uses LUMIO's 10 overlapping hours, not its 60 pooled hours. The v1.2 gate is out-of-sample: three windows (Taurids 11/1-6 and 11/12-17/2026, Geminids 12/13-14/2026) were frozen in public/scoreboard.json before they happen, and are scored only on third-party reports; the v1.2 badge stays INCOMPLETE until at least one is scored. The log-normal sigma is one value for all terms, estimated out of sample from the leave-one-program-out residuals (the shower/sporadic split is not identifiable with 30 sessions) and floored at 0.5, so the bands are wide. v1.1 summary: v1.1 re-ran the gate with fetched data. Bar A: all 12 statements pass, including 7 measured from the TUM Geminids-2025 and Lyrids-2026 map images (lit fraction and night-side impact-capable fraction within 0.10, lit side exact); the maps' orientation is not stated, so sub-radiant angles were NOT scored. Bar B: 26 of 26 scorable hold-out sessions are inside their 90 % interval and pooled observed/expected is 220/208.8 = 1.05, but the log-normal sigma of the fit is 1.36 (bands about x9 wide each way; 11 of the passes are zero-count nights), the Geminid sessions are over-forecast (LUMIO 17 vs 99) and the sporadic background is under-forecast x4.7 against NELIOTA (145 vs 31): the pooled ratio is a cancellation. Banner kept pending review.

model: Expected flashes per hour = detection efficiency x [sum over active showers of k_shower x activity profile x observable fraction + sporadic constant x dark visible area]. The observable fraction is the share of a shower's lunar impacts that land on the Earth-facing night side (cos chi weighting with the horizon cut, Madiedo et al. 2015 eq. 4), from the Moon's real position, phase and libration. Efficiency is 1 for the NASA 0.35 m program that sets the units; every other observing program (MIDAS, UEC, NELIOTA, TILT, LUMIO) has its own fitted efficiency, shrunk toward an aperture law (aperture/0.35 m)^1.5, and the public scope classes (30-40 cm, 20 cm, 10 cm) carry a class efficiency with its own uncertainty (20 cm and 10 cm are aperture extrapolations; 10 cm is flagged). k for the Geminids, Taurids (northern branch tied to the southern), Lyrids and Perseids and the sporadic constant are fitted to 30 published sessions; every other shower is provisional (scaled from the Geminids, x3 band). Bands are 90 % model bands (log-normal, one sigma for every term, estimated out of sample by leaving each observing program out in turn and floored at 0.5); a count over N hours is further Poisson-scattered. Rates assume your field covers the dark side as the calibration programs' did. Not fully validated.
disclosure: Computed by AI build threads (v1: Claude Opus 5.5; v1.1 data verification: Claude Sonnet 5.5; v1.2 per-program model: Claude Opus 5.5, v1.2 sigma and publication: Claude Sonnet 5.5, with specs and rulings by Claude Fable 5.1; Anthropic) for Jonathan Carroll's ResearchJobs project; the model, data and gate are in the repository. Not reviewed by a lunar-impact specialist. Expected rates are model estimates, not observations.

30-40cm.basis: fitted: mean ln-efficiency of NASA 0.35 m, MIDAS 0.36 m, TILT 0.40 m (each scaled to 0.35 m); sigma = their sample SD

20cm.basis: no program at 20 cm: 30-40 cm class x (0.20/0.35)^1.5, sigma = sqrt(sigma_30^2 + tau^2) (prior, widened)

10cm.basis: no program at 10 cm: 30-40 cm class x (0.10/0.35)^1.5, sigma = sqrt(sigma_30^2 + tau^2); extrapolated
